I shut the unnecessary-remarks department with my fist.

Privately, haan, some agreement was there.

On a park bench, of all places, the man sat with his back perfectly straight. Not stiff, though. He had probably kept that posture so long that it was his body's ordinary arrangement.

Was that why he was tall?

Then my slouch... meri height ka chor? Was I stealing my own height? Uff. Possible. Horribly possible.

A magnificent lump stood on his forehead. Cool it, and it should heal soon enough, but still. Put that lump on MY head and then ask for forgiveness without one complaint. Dekhte hain. Let us see.

His heart had room mine simply did not.

The Silver Star incidents. They had begun about two years ago.

A village. A school. A military base. Somewhere full of people, and then suddenly—finished. So brutally, and with no sense to be made of it.

Everybody dead. Sab ke sab.

Some cut down. Some beaten all over. Some bodies cut apart with impossible skill, others torn to pieces.

Here, it looked as if a terrifying killer had ended a life with one stroke. There, as if people had lost their minds and killed one another.

Looked. Seemed. Kya hua tha? What had actually happened?

People died. The disaster left its marks, but no shape you could give to the thing that had caused it.

Why had they died? What had killed them?

Silence answering silence.

Who was going to tell you, bhai? Everybody was dead. Not one person left.

A few uncertain accounts, bas. That was what there was.

—Something flew away from the village where it happened.
—A figure walked away, the school burning behind it.
—Something silver went across the sky just then.
—Even warriors are dead! Then whoever did it must be...

This was how Yamato came to know there was something.

A killer. Silver. A killer of warriors.

The Silver Warrior!
The Celestial Sign of Slaughter!
The Meteor of Calamity!

SILVER STAR!

Violence that left nobody alive. Destruction that brought even warriors down. A nightmare doing equal justice like a god.

Huge or small? Pata nahin.
From Yamato or from abroad? Nobody knew.
Sane or mad? That also, nobody knew.

But silver. Haan. Silver.

Some unknown silver warrior was destroying villages, towns, military forts. Those were the Silver Star incidents.

In the two years since they began, seven cases had been confirmed across Kanto. Rokuhara had its dedicated investigators. GHQ had its own.

Solution chhodo. They hadn't even found where to begin.

Of course he couldn't. Ismein sochna kya tha? What was there to think about?

Rokuhara commanded all Yamato's warriors. Strongest force in the country. Nobody could stand against it.

If there was one exception—

Then that was this unidentified warrior called Silver Star. The silver killer. A monster that made prey of Rokuhara itself.

Believe the rumours that slipped past the Shogunate's controls, and Silver Star had wiped out a whole company of Rokuhara warriors.

Akela. Alone.

True or false, I didn't know. But with Silver Star, Rokuhara's usual arrogant leisure was nowhere to be seen. One doubtful piece of information, off the investigators ran. Another one, off in the other direction.

As if Rokuhara itself was frightened.

Apparently, some of the anti-Shogunate people scattered across Yamato called Silver Star a hero for that.

...Aur the ordinary civilians it killed? Them also somebody should count.

Silver Star, the Rain of Death!

What it really was, we didn't know. But if one warrior truly brushed Rokuhara aside like that, then number one in the world. No argument left.

Nobody could win.

Jeetna possible hi nahin tha. It just wasn't possible.

But thande dimaag se. Cool the head and look properly. Our Rokuhara conspiracy had exactly zero evidence. Even the warrior sighting wasn't certain.
